newsitem.title: INDIA: Blue chips lead slide, Bombay index off 3.62 pct.
newsitem.headline: Blue chips lead slide, Bombay index off 3.62 pct.

text.p: A major sell-off in blue chips on Tuesday pushed the Bombay index down by 156 points, the biggest fall in nearly five months, traders said. The Bombay index ended 3.62 percent down at a provisional 4,164.62.
The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) reopened on Tuesday following a four day break.
And the selling pressure on the Bombay bourse was mostly in line with Monday's fall of more than two percent on the National Stock Exchange, traders said.
"There were very few buyers today. Suddenly, sellers seemed to outnumber buyers at a time when holidays played the spoil-sport," said the head of dealing at a foreign brokerage.
The 156 points or 3.62 percent drop on Tuesday helped Bombay shares extend a three-day old correction as buyers continued to stay on the sidelines amid lack of positive news.
"There were no takers even at lower levels. But, I believe there could be a temporary halt to the slide," said Hitesh Sheth, chief dealer at brokers Prabhudas Lilladher Pvt Ltd.

Some U.S. based funds were among the major sellers on Tuesday following Friday's near record market plunge when the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 250 points. The index however, jumped 109 points on Monday as bargain hunters stepped in.
Back home, the Bombay index fall was the biggest after a nearly 300 point-or-eight percent tumble in March this year.

But investors should see falling prices as an opportunity to buy, Caspian Research India Pvt Ltd said. "The volatility of the next four to five months should be viewed as opportunity to accumulate stock," the securities firm said in its latest report.
The fall in share prices is a logical correction after the benchmark Bombay Stock Exchange index had soared 60 percent from a three-year low reached in December 1996, it said.
